_comment: The one copy of every client recipe. The admin UI renders these with this gateway's real address and live model list; scripts/gen-client-docs.py renders them into docs/clients.md with example values, and `make check` fails if that file is stale. Edit here, never in either output. A client may also carry "downloads", served from the binary at /admin/tools/<name> and staged there from scripts/ by `make tools`. A snippet with a "filename" gets a download button, which matters because the clipboard API is unavailable over plain HTTP. Placeholders: {{base}} the gateway base URL with no trailing slash, {{model}} a capable model, {{smallModel}} a cheap one, {{models}} crush's generated model array.

clients.label: Claude Code
clients.lead: No `/v1` — Claude Code appends the path itself. Use `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` rather than `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`: it is the variable the client documents for a custom base URL.

snippets.label: Environment

notes: The two model variables are optional — without them Claude Code discovers models through `/v1/models`, which the gateway proxies. Set them to pin a model, and keep the small one small: it runs many times a session for titles and summaries.

clients.label: Codex CLI
clients.lead: With `/v1`, and this is the one client that goes through the OpenAI Responses API rather than the Anthropic one. `wire_api = "responses"` is not optional — Responses is the only wire format Codex has, and `chat_completions` appears nowhere in its binary.

snippets.label: ~/.codex/config.toml
snippets.template:
model_provider = "claudication"
model = "{{model}}"
model_catalog_json = "~/.codex/claude-models.json"

[model_providers.claudication]
name = "claudication"
base_url = "{{base}}/v1"
env_key = "CLAUDICATION_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"

notes: `env_key` names an environment variable, not a key — putting `clc_…` there directly does not work.
Set `model` to a Claude model. Codex asks for `gpt-5-codex` by default, which means nothing upstream, and the gateway then substitutes whatever `openai.model` says.

Codex looks its model up in a catalog compiled into its own binary, and a Claude name is not in it — so it falls back to conservative limits and a million-token model starts shedding context early. The catalog above fixes that, with an entry per model the gateway serves.

One caveat, measured rather than assumed: Codex refuses a catalog entry carrying neither `base_instructions` nor `model_messages.instructions_template`, so every catalog must contain a system prompt. The one above is a short stand-in, because Codex's own lives in its binary and nothing here can read it. That costs about nine thousand tokens of Codex's editing and formatting instructions per turn — cheaper, and less good at editing. Download the script below instead to clone the real prompt out of your own Codex.

Codex needs `bubblewrap` installed before it can run any shell command. Without it the first tool call panics and the model then explains, convincingly, that nothing works — which reads like a broken tool bridge and is not one.

downloads.name: codex-model-catalog.py
downloads.label: codex-model-catalog.py
downloads.what: Writes the same catalog, but cloned from your own Codex binary, so it carries Codex's real system prompt rather than the stand-in above. Run it on the machine Codex is installed on: `python3 codex-model-catalog.py --codex $(which codex)`.

clients.label: opencode
clients.lead: With `/v1`. It overrides the built-in Anthropic provider rather than declaring a new one, so every model the gateway serves is available without listing any of them.
notes: If opencode announces a model from some other vendor at startup, it is not using this provider at all and a stale key elsewhere is winning. Read what it prints before believing a test that passed.

clients.label: crush
clients.lead: Without `/v1`, and every model has to be spelled out: crush never calls `/v1/models`, so one absent from this file cannot be selected however well the gateway serves it. The Setup tab generates the whole stanza from the live model list.
notes: The zero costs are deliberate. A subscription is not billed per token, and leaving real prices in makes crush display a running total that is fiction.
The context windows are a best guess per model. They affect what crush displays and when it truncates, never what the gateway will serve.

clients.label: curl
clients.lead: For checking the plumbing without a client in the way. Both APIs accept either credential header.

snippets.label: Every model this gateway can serve

shell.what: Mint an API key. The same thing the API keys tab does, for a provisioning script.
Reset the admin password. The recovery path when it is lost — no old password needed.
A single-use link that signs a browser in without typing the password. Spent the first time it is used.
A consistent snapshot without stopping the service. Holds the sealing key and every stored token, so it is exactly as sensitive as the state directory.

troubleshooting.cause: Almost always the `/v1` question. Claude Code and crush want the base URL without it; opencode and Codex want it with. Neither says so when it is wrong.

troubleshooting.symptom: 404 saying the API is turned off
troubleshooting.cause: That surface is switched off under Settings → API surfaces. The message names which one.
The key is wrong, revoked, or in a header this client does not send. Either `x-api-key` or a bearer token works, on either API.

troubleshooting.symptom: 429 whose message is the single word "Error"
troubleshooting.cause: Not a rate limit. The subscription backend refuses opus and sonnet to anything that is not Claude Code, and says so misleadingly. Leave `passthrough.claude-code-attribution` on and it is handled for you.

troubleshooting.symptom: "Third-party apps now draw from your extra usage"
troubleshooting.cause: Also not a billing message. A content check refused the request. The Usage tab labels these; `scripts/bisect-refusal.py` finds the trigger.

troubleshooting.symptom: Only haiku works; opus and sonnet 429
troubleshooting.cause: The same attribution gate, seen from the other side.

troubleshooting.symptom: A model works in one client and not another
troubleshooting.cause: The gateway does not filter models, so this is the client: crush needs every model listed in its own config, and Codex needs one in its catalog. The others discover them.
The gateway sends a terminal event on every path, including failures — so this points at something between it and Codex, usually a proxy buffering the stream.
